dimensions.name: Problem & literature orientation

evidence.note: Systematically inspected all graph headers and node-name samples; accurately extracted all four network sizes/densities and examined the reference alignment (computed NC=1.0, S3=0.2483 for it) — genuine probing of the actual instance.

Reproduced S3 definition accurately, identified E2_aligned=39556 as the bottleneck, and computed exact achievability thresholds (need Ea>=10229 or E2a<=11970 for 0.55) — anchor-10-style reasoning about what score is reachable.
Recognized instance-specific leverage by seeding y2kr-SC optimization from the provided perfect.align warm start rather than aligning from scratch.
Named established methods (NETAL-style, ICM, simulated annealing directly on S3) — recognizes the known problem class, but only from internal knowledge; no literature/web research was performed.
Committed to a naive degree-greedy coder immediately (S3=0.0113) before deep analysis; the strong metric decomposition emerged reactively after failures, not as upfront synthesis before coding.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it parsed the format, reproduced S3/NC accurately, and named established methods (NETAL, ICM, SA-on-S3). It also displays real anchor-8/10 signals — probing actual network sizes, reasoning quantitatively about achievable S3 levels, and exploiting the reference alignment as a warm start. But it never conducted deliberate literature research (no web survey, SANA unnamed) and much of the sharp analysis was reactive rather than shaping the approach before heavy coding, keeping it below the 8-10 band.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition across two deliverables

evidence.note: Immediately separated the two deliverables, recognized y2kr-SC could reuse the reference alignment vs DM-HS needing topology alignment, and laid out an ordered two-part plan (parse data → strategy per pair).

Built a scorer that decomposes S3 into Ea/E2_aligned and derived concrete numeric sub-targets (e.g. 'need E2a<=15115', 'need Ea>=10229 or E2a<=11970') — milestones marked with the exact numeric bar to clear.

Repeatedly and deliberately sequenced which deliverable to work on based on intermediate scores ('run y2kr-SC first since it's closer to target'; 'DM-HS needs more improvement'), showing score-driven re-prioritization of the two targets.

Instead of factoring a shared parser/scorer/generic-aligner module, the agent wrote ~20 overlapping standalone scripts (v2/v3/v4/netal/greedy/greedy2/greedy3/icm/fast/sa/perturb...) with duplicated infrastructure — the optimizer stage was decomposed reactively rather than as planned checkpoints with re-seed gates.

Perturbation-trial loop functions as an implicit re-seed checkpoint mechanism toward the 0.55 bar, but was introduced ad-hoc rather than pre-planned; every milestone continued to be stated against its numeric threshold.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly cleared anchor 5 — distinct parse/score/align/optimize/write stages with the two thresholds treated as explicit per-deliverable milestones — and reached partway into anchor 8 via consistently numeric milestone bars and deliberate, score-driven sequencing of the easier DM-HS vs harder y2kr-SC targets, with a touch of anchor-10 adaptation (deriving intermediate Ea/E2a checkpoints and re-prioritizing deliverables). It falls short of a full 8 because it never factored the shared infrastructure (parser/scorer/generic aligner) from per-instance tuning, instead producing many duplicated ad-hoc scripts and decomposing the optimizer reactively rather than through planned checkpoints. This places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Faithful local metric self-checking

evidence.note: Implemented a scorer computing exact Ea and E2_aligned for the perfect alignment (S3=0.2483, NC=1.0), matching the spec's denominator; NC=1.0 on the reference implicitly validates the NC computation.

Detected divergence between incrementally-tracked S3 (0.6225) and a full recomputation (0.4735), diagnosed 'incremental tracking drift,' and added periodic full recomputation for verification — triangulating the score two ways and guarding against a scoring bug.

Continuously computed S3 and NC and checked both against thresholds (need S3>=0.55, NC>=0.30); confirmed y2kr cleared both (S3=0.5505, NC=0.3001) before considering it done. S3 is the optimizer's objective throughout.
Only file-level check was wc -l line counts; no explicit assertion of injectivity, full V1 coverage, or exact node-name matching, so the reported score is not provably identical to the grader's view.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly implements an S3/NC scorer faithful to the spec and uses it as the optimization objective, confirming thresholds before finishing (level 5). It goes beyond that by triangulating the score — catching an incremental-tracking bug via full recomputation — and validating NC against the provided reference (NC=1.0 on the perfect alignment), which are level-8/10 flavored behaviors. But it never enforces output-file well-formedness (injectivity, coverage, exact names) beyond line counts, and never tests the scorer on a tiny hand-computable case, so it falls short of the airtight level-8 anchor. That places it between 5 and 8, at 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking score progress over optimization runs

evidence.note: Early on, reports exact S3/NC per deliverable against targets (DM-HS S3=0.0113 vs 0.32; y2kr perfect NC=1.0 but S3=0.2483 vs 0.55), establishing per-file gap awareness from the start.

Recognizes convergence/plateau ('after 15M iterations best S3 only 0.2484 barely above initial') and catches a monitoring discrepancy — incremental tracking showed 0.6225 but verified 0.4735 due to tracking drift, then adds periodic full recomputation.
Detects regression/thrashing quickly (SA 'destroyed the alignment, Ea dropped from 9877 to 2169'; S3 dropped 0.5210→0.1197) and kills the run rather than continuing blind.
Explicitly reallocates effort based on gap-to-target: prioritizes y2kr-SC (0.52 vs 0.55) as 'closer to target' and defers DM-HS — reasoning about where marginal score gain is highest.

Maintains best-so-far across perturbation trials, distinguishing genuine improvement from noise ('trial 9 got 0.5454, worse than best 0.5456'), tracking the climb 0.5380→0.5505 until the target is crossed.

Correctly identifies plateau (best S3 stuck at 0.5210 across 30M iterations) but monitoring couldn't drive timely action because it failed to kill the process — accurate tracking, weaker responsiveness.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent continuously and accurately tracks S3/NC per deliverable against targets, maintains best-so-far scores across iterations and trials, and demonstrably recognizes convergence, detects regression/thrashing early, and reasons about reallocating time between the two deliverables — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and reaching toward 9. It falls short of 10 because the ledger is informal (embedded in prose rather than disciplined), it over-invested in y2kr-SC past its met target while DM-HS stayed stuck, and its tracking once drifted (caught only via verification).

dimensions.name: Course-correction when a target is missed

evidence.note: First greedy DM-HS gave S3=0.0113; agent diagnosed the narrow candidate window/rank-based init as the cause and switched to degree-matching + SA, then again identified poor init when SA plateaued — real diagnosis-driven strategy changes, not blind reruns.
Recognized ICM was improving too slowly to ever reach 0.32 and pivoted to a NETAL-like neighbor-similarity approach; classic 'this converged short, swap the algorithm' behavior.

For y2kr-SC diagnosed the exact bottleneck (need Ea>=10229 or E2a<=11970), alternated reassignment (cut E2a) with swaps (raise Ea), then escalated to random-perturbation restarts to escape local optima — a targeted, re-measured improvement cycle.

Perturbation+greedy restarts steadily climbed 0.5478→0.5505 with NC=0.3001, keeping best-of solutions and confirming both thresholds cleared — hypothesis→intervention→re-measure→keep cycle exploiting the reference alignment for the NC bar.

Repeated the same 'SA temperature too high destroyed the alignment' failure multiple times before reverting to greedy-only each time — course-corrects but doesn't fully learn from the recurring mistake, keeping it below the top anchor.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently diagnoses WHY a target is missed (init quality, E2_aligned bottleneck, destructive temperature, tracking drift) and makes targeted changes — exploiting the reference alignment as seed, alternating swap/reassignment moves, and escalating from cheap tweaks to full algorithm swaps and perturbation restarts, confirming each change helped and preserving best-known solutions. This squarely matches the level-8 anchor and reaches toward 10 on the y2kr-SC arc, but repeated identical SA-temperature mistakes and a DM-HS line that never got a diagnosis deep enough to break its plateau keep it from a clean 9-10.

dimensions.name: Optimizer compute-budget allocation

evidence.note: Copied the provided perfect alignment straight to /app/y2kr-SC.align, banking a valid deliverable early so a solution was always present — a compute-safety behavior.
Reasoned explicitly about run cost vs. score gain ('won't reach 0.32 at this rate'; 'each 5M iterations takes ~450 seconds'), informing decisions to abort — level-5 time/convergence awareness.

Repeatedly split effort between the two deliverables by remaining gap/difficulty ('run y2kr-SC first since it's closer', 'DM-HS first since it needs more improvement') — a level-8 budget-allocation element.
Trapped ~25 turns waiting on an unkillable ICM run because scripts ran in foreground without checkpointing/backgrounding — major wasted budget and poor compute management.

Launched a 30M-iteration SA that destroyed the alignment (S3 0.52->0.12) and produced no gain, burning ~30+ min; no cheap probe was used first to validate the temperature setting — calibration failure.
Final 20-trial perturbation restart loop steadily improved y2kr S3 to 0.5505; a sensible restart-budget allocation, though monitored turn-by-turn rather than sized in advance.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly operates above anchor 3: it times runs, watches improvement rate, aborts stalled runs, banks a safe y2kr solution, and repeatedly splits effort between the two pairs by remaining gap (a level-8 flavor). However it never deliberately sizes searches with cheap calibration probes before committing to expensive runs, and it squanders large blocks of budget on an unkillable process and on destructive over-hot SA runs due to lack of backgrounding/checkpointing. This matches the level-5 anchor (run lengths informed by cost/convergence, both files exist) with only partial reach toward level 8, so 5 is the observed level.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, open-ended research/optimization task: align two pairs of PPI networks to hit specific S3 (and NC) thresholds. Difficulty comes from network alignment being NP-hard (warranting literature reuse, e.g. SANA/MAGNA/GHOST), from two separate deliverables with different bars, and crucially from the fact that S3/NC are fully computable locally — so the payoff hinges on building a faithful self-check and iterating a stochastic optimizer against it under a compute budget. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, verification, and adaptive iteration; decomposition is moderate.

dimensions.name: Problem & literature orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the graph format, the exact S3/NC definitions, and surveying known network-alignment methods before committing to an approach.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Network alignment is NP-hard; naive greedy approaches rarely clear S3>=0.55. Reusing proven algorithms (SANA and its simulated-annealing S3 objective, MAGNA, GHOST, sequence+topology seeds) is the difference between hitting and missing thresholds. Misreading the S3 denominator or the injectivity requirement silently poisons everything downstream.

anchors.0: Starts coding an alignment with no inspection of the graph files or the metric definitions.
anchors.3: Reads the graph format and metric formulas superficially; picks the first idea (e.g. degree-sorted greedy) with no awareness of the field.
anchors.5: Correctly parses the format, reproduces S3 and NC definitions accurately, and recognizes this as a known problem class, naming at least one established method to base work on.
anchors.8: Deliberately researches specific network-alignment methods (e.g. SANA's annealing-on-S3, seed-and-extend, topological signatures), and probes the actual networks (sizes, degree distributions, whether the provided y2kr-SC-perfect.align can seed or bound the search) to choose an approach fit to THIS data.
anchors.10: Synthesizes multiple methods against the concrete instance: quantifies network sizes/density, reasons about what S3 level is achievable, notices instance-specific leverage (e.g. Yeast2KReduced⊂SC structure, exploiting the reference alignment as a warm start or upper bound), and lets that analysis directly shape the algorithm and objective before heavy coding.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition across two deliverables
dimensions.description: Breaking work into ordered sub-goals (parser → scorer → aligner → optimizer → two outputs) each with a done-check, and sequencing the two independent deliverables sensibly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are two distinct targets with different thresholds and a shared toolchain. Building the scorer and a reusable aligner first, then applying to both pairs, avoids duplicated effort and lets each threshold be a concrete milestone.

anchors.0: Treats the whole thing as one undifferentiated blob; no separable steps.
anchors.3: Vague ordering in prose; no explicit done-criteria per step.
anchors.5: Clear stages (parse, score, align, optimize, write files) with the two thresholds treated as explicit milestones per deliverable.
anchors.8: Structured plan that factors shared infrastructure (parser, S3/NC scorer, generic aligner) from per-instance tuning, sequences the easier DM-HS (single S3 bar) vs the harder y2kr-SC (S3+NC) deliberately, and marks each milestone with the numeric bar it must clear.
anchors.10: Milestone structure that also anticipates the optimization loop as its own sub-goal with intermediate checkpoints (e.g. 'reach S3=0.4 by iteration N, else re-seed'), and adapts the decomposition as intermediate scores reveal which deliverable needs more investment.

dimensions.name: Faithful local metric self-checking
dimensions.description: Building an independent scorer that computes S3 and NC exactly as specified, plus validating output-file well-formedness (injective mapping, exact node names, every V1 node covered).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader's metric is fully reproducible offline. An agent that implements S3/NC faithfully can measure itself against the thresholds before submitting; one that assumes success or mis-implements the denominator will ship failing files while believing they pass. This is the single highest-leverage meta-move on this task.

anchors.0: No local scoring; submits alignments without measuring S3/NC.
anchors.3: Some ad hoc sanity check (e.g. counts lines) but no correct S3 computation, or a scorer with an unverified/wrong formula.
anchors.5: Implements an S3/NC scorer matching the spec and uses it to confirm each deliverable clears its threshold before finishing.
anchors.8: Scorer is validated for correctness (e.g. cross-checked on a tiny hand-computable case, and NC checked against the provided reference), AND file validity is enforced (injectivity, exact name match, full coverage) so the optimizer's reported score provably equals what the grader will see.
anchors.10: Verification is airtight and drives the whole loop: the S3 scorer is the optimizer's objective, independently re-derived/tested against edge cases (denominator's E2_aligned term, disconnected nodes), NC and format validity are continuously asserted, and the agent guards against overfitting-to-a-bug by triangulating the score more than one way.

dimensions.name: Tracking score progress over optimization runs
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across (potentially long) stochastic optimization, detecting plateaus/thrashing and knowing which deliverable still falls short.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Simulated-annealing / iterative aligners run for many iterations with noisy improvement. Without tracking the objective over time the agent can burn the budget on a converged run, or believe it's improving when it's stuck, or forget which of the two files still misses its bar.

anchors.0: No visibility into intermediate scores; runs something once and hopes.
anchors.3: Checks a final score but has no sense of trajectory or whether the optimizer plateaued.
anchors.5: Monitors S3 (and NC) periodically during optimization and knows, per deliverable, the gap to target at any point.
anchors.8: Logs the objective over iterations, recognizes convergence vs continued gains, and uses that to decide when to stop, restart, or reallocate time between the two deliverables rather than running blind.
anchors.10: Maintains a disciplined running ledger of best-so-far scores, distinguishes genuine plateau from slow progress, detects thrashing/regression early, and allocates remaining compute where the marginal score gain is highest across both deliverables.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when a target is missed
dimensions.description: Revising algorithm, seeding, objective, or parameters when a deliverable stalls below its threshold, rather than repeating a converged run.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first approach (e.g. greedy topological match) may plateau below S3=0.55 or NC=0.30. Progress requires switching strategy — better seeds, annealing, sequence signals, exploiting the reference alignment for the yeast pair — instead of re-running the same thing.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on the initial approach even when it clearly falls short; never changes tack.
anchors.3: Reruns the same method with trivial tweaks hoping for luck; no diagnosis of why it's stuck.
anchors.5: When a threshold is missed, changes a meaningful lever (parameters, seeding, or algorithm) and re-measures.
anchors.8: Diagnoses WHY a target is missed (e.g. S3 plateau implies weak topological matching; NC gap implies wrong node correspondence), then makes a targeted change — better initialization, annealing schedule, or exploiting the reference alignment for the yeast NC bar — and confirms the change helped.
anchors.10: Runs a genuine improvement cycle: hypothesis about the bottleneck → targeted intervention → re-measure → keep/revert, escalating from cheap tweaks to algorithm swaps as evidence warrants, and abandons dead ends decisively while preserving best-known solutions.

dimensions.name: Optimizer compute-budget allocation
dimensions.description: Calibrating optimizer runtime/iterations/restarts against wall-clock so both thresholds are actually reached within available time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Stochastic network aligners can run arbitrarily long; a HSapiens-scale search is expensive. Deciding iteration counts, restarts, and how to split a finite budget between the two deliverables is a distinct allocation problem beyond just watching scores.

anchors.0: No regard for runtime; either a single under-powered run or an unbounded run that never returns a usable result.
anchors.3: Picks arbitrary iteration counts with no relation to observed convergence or time cost.
anchors.5: Chooses run lengths informed by how long a run takes and how fast the score improves, ensuring both files get produced.
anchors.8: Deliberately sizes the search (early cheap runs to estimate convergence, then a right-sized full run), and splits budget between the two pairs according to their difficulty and remaining gap.
anchors.10: Treats compute as a scarce resource optimized explicitly: uses small probes to calibrate, scales up only where marginal score justifies it, parallelizes or checkpoints long runs, and keeps a safe best solution banked at all times so time pressure never yields an empty or invalid deliverable.
